title: Business-value alignment
task_statement: Price a Claude solution with baseline cost, new cost, and error cost, and set guards on quality and spend. (Inference: wording from secondary sources)

components.name: Unit cost from published prices
components.first_principle: The cost of one request follows from its token counts and the published price per million tokens.

nodes.label: Request with prompt and expected output

steps: Use the token count endpoint to measure the input tokens of a typical request.
Multiply the input tokens by the input price per million tokens.
Multiply the output tokens by the output price per million tokens.
Apply the batch discount when the work can wait.
Compare the usage fields in responses with the estimate.
pros: The unit cost follows directly from published prices.
Batch processing halves the token cost for work that can wait.
Cache hits cost a fraction of the base input price.
cons: Prices change with the model and with the prompt length.
Output length can differ from the estimate. (Inference)
Token counts vary with the input content. (Inference)
use_when: A business case needs a cost per request.
The team compares two models on cost per task.
do_not_use_when: The team has no volume estimate, so no annual figure can follow. (Inference)
The estimate uses a price from a source other than the published price table. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Start with Claude Haiku 5.5, which the docs list for the lowest latency and price.
constraints.combination: Compare a larger model only when evals show a gap in quality.

constraints.choice: On Claude Haiku 5.5, keep prompts at or under 100,000 tokens when price is the main concern.
constraints.combination: Use prompt caching for a long, stable prefix. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Check the platform rate limits before you size the volume.
constraints.combination: Request a higher quota only after you measure the peak load. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name the owner who signs the cost estimate. (Inference)

components.exam_tie: D1.6. Expect a business case with several terms. The credited answer prices each term with a number and names the owner of the estimate. (Inference)
components.trap: A savings claim with one term, such as labor saved, and no build or run cost. The total looks positive and leaves out cost. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Price the unit cost from the published rates, then multiply it by the expected volume.
components.exam_tip: If the stem gives no price, write Not in source and state the price as an assumption. (Inference)

components.name: Value guards for quality and spend
components.first_principle: A value claim holds only while its quality threshold and its spend cap still hold. (Inference)
steps: Set a quality threshold on the eval set before you price the change.
Set a spend ceiling for each run or session.
Configure a session budget so that the platform stops new model requests at the cap, and the session pauses.
Record the pass rate and the spend with each release.
Re-sign the value estimate when the volume or the error mix changes.
pros: The guards stop a cost cut that lowers quality. (Inference)
A session budget caps spend for the session, runs included.
The owner signs figures that come from measured results. (Inference)
cons: The threshold needs an eval set that matches real traffic. (Inference)
A budget pauses the session at the cap, so the task waits until you raise or remove the budget.
Thresholds need review as the models change. (Inference)
use_when: Finance asks for the return on a model change.
A quality failure has a financial cost. (Inference)
do_not_use_when: A prototype runs with no users and no spend. (Inference)
No eval set exists, so no pass rate can be measured. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Track the list cost and token usage of each session.
Set a session budget before each long run.
constraints.combination: Set a lower budget for runs with fixed steps. (Inference)

constraints.choice: Name one owner for each threshold. (Inference)
Check the platform rate limits before a volume increase. (Inference)

native_services.text: Session budgets are a Managed Agents feature in beta. Budget support on each native platform: Not in source.

components.exam_tie: D1.6. Expect a value question where a cut in one term hides a quality loss. The credited answer keeps a quality threshold next to the value math. (Inference)
components.trap: A latency cut that breaks the quality threshold. The number looks like value, but the error cost moves in the other direction. (Inference)
components.decision_rule: Keep each value claim only while its quality threshold and its spend cap hold.
components.exam_tip: If a stem reports a speed gain, check the quality threshold before you count the gain as value. (Inference)

key_facts.text: A session budget is an optional hard spend ceiling that you set when you create a session.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The platform prices session consumption at public list rates.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: The platform stops new model requests once the session list cost reaches the budget.
key_facts.label: Fact

key_facts.text: A session at its budget pauses and goes idle, and a change or removal of the budget resumes the work.
key_facts.label: Fact

decision_flow:
flowchart TD
  A{Quality threshold met on eval set?} -->|No| X[Do not ship the change]
  A -->|Yes| B{Spend under session cap?}
  B -->|No| C[Cut tokens per task or volume]
  B -->|Yes| D{Net value positive with all terms?}
  D -->|No| X
  D -->|Yes| E[Owner signs the estimate]
cheatsheet:
flowchart LR
  B[Baseline cost] --> N[Net value]
  W[New unit cost] --> N
  E[Error cost avoided] --> N
  BU[Build and run cost] --> N
  N --> Q{Quality threshold}
  Q -->|Pass| O[Owner signs]
  Q -->|Fail| X[No sign-off]

patterns.wording: a savings claim with one term
patterns.rule: Count the baseline, the new cost, the errors avoided, and the build and run cost.
traps: Adjectives such as faster or better with no figure

patterns.wording: a model change that lowers cost
patterns.answer_type: cost change with a quality threshold
patterns.rule: Keep the cost change only while the eval pass rate holds.
traps: Cost cut with no quality check

patterns.wording: a spend overrun risk on long agent runs
patterns.rule: Set a session budget before the run starts.
traps: Cap set after the bill arrives
Lower model tier as the only spend control

not_in_source: Quality threshold value for any product: Not in source.
